speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia. To understand the underlying cause, could you tell me when your balance issues first started and if they have been getting worse over time? Also, do you experience any weakness, numbness, or changes in your speech or vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the asymmetry in your limbs is a crucial clue. Can you tell me if you have any history of cancer, autoimmune disorders, or if you've noticed any recent weight loss? Additionally, have you experienced any changes in your vision or coordination when lying down?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) due to natalizumab therapy in a patient with Crohn's disease.

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast.
REQUEST IMAGES: T2/FLAIR sequences of the brain.

Please describe any new visual disturbances, such as blind spots or field cuts, and confirm if you have been experiencing recent fatigue or confusion alongside your worsening ataxia.
